rationale.steemAskStepBps: askStep 80→60bps: the drift-protection that justified 80bps (9-c) is now mechanical — the value-guard cancels any sub-parity ask every beat (measured 5 cancels in run 39723306632), so max adverse-selection exposure is drift between ~3s beats, not 4-day drift. 60bps keeps expected maker edge >= 0 by construction (value line) while moving level-1 ask 20bps closer to the touch; cost floor (avgCost+100bps) still overrides when basis demands.
rationale.steemBidStepBps: bidStep 150→100bps: fill requires a >=1% dip instead of 1.5% — expected fill odds roughly +50% per level on the same tape; every fill still lands >= ~+100bps surplus vs drifted parity (the dip itself remains the adverse-selection price paid, now bounded tighter by weekly range ~77bps measured).

rationale.levels: 3x3 kept: book depth is thin (touch sizes ≈ tens of STEEM); more levels fragment the queue and raise RC burn per refresh without measurable fill gain on a book that traded 72 fills in 38 days.
rationale.hiveAskMinRecvHbd: 0.2 HBD kept — R99 measured price-fidelity law unchanged; HIVE leg stays honestly inventory-gated (0.034 HIVE / 0.003 HBD live) until fills accumulate price-grade fuel.
rationale.expectedFill: STEEM: bid side expected 0.1–0.4 fills/week per level at 150bps (σ_daily ≈ 11bps measured, weekly range ≈ 77bps); ask side fills concentrate at level-1 (touch) ≈ 0.5–2/week when SBD demand lifts. rationale.honesty: fill-rate figures are estimates from a 72-fill tape and 7-day parity series, not promises; the ledger keeps marking every fill's live edge (marked-at-detection) so the next proposal re-fits from receipts.
